# statusdrift_monitor (Resource)

Manages a StatusDrift monitor.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "statusdrift_monitor" "api_health" {
  name          = "API Health Check"
  type          = "HTTPS"
  url           = "https://api.example.com/health"
  interval      = 5
  enabled       = true
  location_type = "region"
  region        = "us-east-1"

  http_method          = "GET"
  expected_status_code = "200"
  max_redirects        = 3
  rw_timeout           = 10
  connection_timeout   = 10

  monitor_group_id = statusdrift_monitor_group.production.id
  tag_ids          = [statusdrift_tag.critical.id]

  locations_down_to_alert = 1
  checks_down_to_alert    = 2
  warning_threshold_ms    = 5000

  alert {
    notification_channel_ids   = [statusdrift_notification_channel.slack_alerts.id]
    conditions                 = ["down", "warning"]
    delay_minutes              = 2
    enabled                    = true
    recurring_interval_minutes = 15
    max_recurrences            = 5
    notify_on_call             = true
    on_call_policy_id          = statusdrift_on_call_policy.default.id
  }

  assertion {
    type           = "json_path"
    expression     = "$.status"
    comparison     = "equals"
    expected_value = "healthy"
  }

  assertion {
    type       = "regex"
    expression = "\"status\"\\s*:\\s*\"healthy\""
    comparison = "matches"
  }
}

resource "statusdrift_monitor" "dns_check" {
  name                = "DNS Monitor"
  type                = "DNS"
  interval            = 60
  enabled             = true
  location_type       = "region"
  region              = "us-east-1"
  dns_hostname        = "example.com"
  dns_monitoring_mode = "discovery"
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `interval` (Number) The monitoring interval in minutes. Valid values depend on monitor type: non-DNS [0,1,5,10,15,30,60,1440], DNS [60,120,180,240,360,480,720,1440].
- `location_type` (String) Location selection type. Valid values: locations, region.
- `name` (String) The name of the monitor.
- `type` (String) The type of monitor. Valid values: HTTPS, HTTP_KEYWORD, HTTPS_CERT, TCP, UDP, PING, PUSH, DNS.

### Optional

- `alert` (Block List) Alert configuration blocks. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--alert))
- `allow_invalid_certificate` (Boolean) Whether to allow invalid SSL certificates.
- `assertion` (Block List) Response body assertion blocks. Only supported for HTTPS and HTTP_KEYWORD monitor types. Maximum 10 per monitor. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--assertion))
- `cache_buster` (Boolean) Whether to append a cache-busting query parameter.
- `checks_down_to_alert` (Number) Number of consecutive checks that must fail before alerting (1-10).
- `connection_timeout` (Number) Connection timeout in seconds (1-45).
- `dns_hostname` (String) The hostname to perform DNS lookup on. Required for DNS monitor type.
- `dns_monitoring_mode` (String) DNS monitoring mode. Valid values: discovery, manual.
- `dns_servers` (List of String) List of DNS servers to query (max 10).
- `enabled` (Boolean) Whether the monitor is enabled.
- `expected_status_code` (String) The expected HTTP status code (e.g., '200' or '200-299').
- `host` (String) The hostname or IP to monitor. Required for TCP, UDP, and PING monitor types.
- `http_auth` (Boolean) Whether HTTP authentication is enabled.
- `http_content_type` (String) The Content-Type header for POST/PUT/PATCH requests.
- `http_method` (String) The HTTP method to use. Valid values: HEAD, GET, POST, PUT, PATCH, DELETE.
- `http_password` (String, Sensitive) The HTTP authentication password.
- `http_post_body` (String) The body to send with POST/PUT/PATCH requests.
- `http_username` (String, Sensitive) The HTTP authentication username.
- `keyword` (String) The keyword to search for in the response body. Used with HTTP_KEYWORD type.
- `keyword_negation` (Boolean) Whether to negate the keyword check (alert when keyword IS found).
- `location_ids` (List of Number) List of location IDs to check from. Use this or location_names when location_type is 'locations'.
- `location_names` (List of String) List of location keys to check from (e.g. "us-nyc-1", "eu-west-1"). Resolved to IDs via the API. Use this or location_ids when location_type is 'locations'.
- `locations_down_to_alert` (Number) Number of locations that must be down before alerting (1-10).
- `max_redirects` (Number) Maximum number of redirects to follow (0-20).
- `monitor_group_id` (Number) The monitor group ID this monitor belongs to.
- `port` (Number) The port to monitor (10-65535). Required for TCP and UDP monitor types.
- `region` (String) The region to check from. Required when location_type is 'region'.
- `rw_timeout` (Number) Read/write timeout in seconds (1-45).
- `tag_ids` (List of Number) List of tag IDs assigned to this monitor.
- `url` (String) The URL to monitor. Required for HTTPS, HTTP_KEYWORD, and HTTPS_CERT monitor types.
- `warning_threshold_ms` (Number) Response time threshold in milliseconds for warning status (100-60000).

### Read-Only

- `id` (Number) The unique identifier of the monitor.

<a id="nestedblock--alert"></a>
### Nested Schema for `alert`

Required:

- `conditions` (List of String) List of alert conditions.
- `notification_channel_ids` (List of Number) List of notification channel IDs to notify.

Optional:

- `delay_minutes` (Number) Delay in minutes before sending the alert.
- `enabled` (Boolean) Whether this alert is enabled.
- `max_recurrences` (Number) Maximum number of recurring alert notifications.
- `notify_on_call` (Boolean) Whether this alert should trigger the on-call escalation policy.
- `on_call_policy_id` (Number) On-call policy ID to use for this alert. When null and notify_on_call is true, the organization default policy is used.
- `recurring_interval_minutes` (Number) Interval in minutes for recurring alerts.


<a id="nestedblock--assertion"></a>
### Nested Schema for `assertion`

Required:

- `comparison` (String) The comparison operator. Valid values depend on assertion type.
- `expression` (String) The expression to evaluate (JSONPath, XPath, or regex pattern). Maximum 500 characters.
- `type` (String) The assertion type. Valid values: json_path, xpath, regex.

Optional:

- `expected_value` (String) The expected value for comparison. Required for equals, not_equals, contains, not_contains, greater_than, less_than. Maximum 1000 characters.
